task: With member spend-limit enforcement off, make the project-budget API read path return a fixed-mode member's stored override amount instead of the full project budget, keep the aggregate total consistent, and add regression tests.

key_reasoning.reason: One component in one layer: the project-budget router. The rule is inlined three times across two functions (the shared budget-response builder, which feeds eight endpoints, and the members-list endpoint), so it is more than a single-function edit but crosses no layer boundary. Service, repository, response models, provider adapter and runtime sync are untouched.

Six concrete acceptance criteria and an explicit display-only scope. Two light points remain for the plan: whether to fold the three copies into one per-member helper, and stating that the displayed override may differ from the cap live at the provider. The stale inline comment about every member holding the full budget needs updating.

Closest pattern is the existing enforcement-off rule from EPMCDME-12959 in the same router, with matching router tests (namespace fixtures plus a patched settings lookup) that serve as a template for the new fixed and mixed-mode cases, so no test-template bump applies. Scored S rather than XS because it changes a user-visible budget figure, narrows an earlier acceptance criterion, must keep three expressions and the aggregate in agreement, and has a zero-override trap if the branch is written on truthiness instead of allocation mode. No security, performance or schema impact; rollback is a revert. Calibration: the task sits between the bundled XS example epmcdme-10101-add-logging-to-endpoint (6, one file, non-functional) and the S example epmcdme-10102-add-validation-to-form-field (11, three files across API and Service); it is single-layer like the XS example but changes business display logic and adds tests. Total 9 is on the XS/S boundary and stays XS because neither Technical Risk nor Component Scope is XL or above and the existing pattern covers nearly all of the implementation.
